clauses.text: Never PR a feature branch straight into `main`.
Keep this file current in the same PR.
A merge never cuts a tag. `/release` does.
Never add `push` back to a release job's `if:`
Always delete a feature branch as soon as it's merged
Never claim a result you did not observe
clauses.rationale: Honesty about what was verified is the whole house contract. A skill that reports success it did not witness is worse than one that reports nothing.

clauses.text: never ask about anything in it
clauses.rationale: Two questions maximum is only achievable because detection already answered the rest. Asking about a detectable signal is the UX failure that makes a skill feel like a form.

clauses.text: The user should see a short status line and a table, not a scroll of raw command output. Concretely: -

Anything that takes more than a couple of seconds gets one short lowercase line as it starts (`fetching the posting…`, `rendering press + ats-plain…`) so the user sees progress rather than dead air. One line each, not a table.

Not a fetched page, not a source file, not a script's own source. Scripts hand each other *paths*; when you need a file's text in context, use the `Read` tool rather than `cat`, `sed`, `head`, or a `--show` flag. Anything the user already has open somewhere is a wall of text in chat. -

Ad-hoc prose summaries are why runs read inconsistently. Every stage that produces more than one fact reports a table with a fixed column set, declared in this skill's own steps below. Omit noise: don't list unchanged fields, don't repeat inputs back, don't show paths the user can't act on. -

Never answer ungrounded: every fact this skill emits carries the file and line it was read from, a fact that loses its source is dropped rather than shown, and a question the cards cannot ground is answered by the retrieval command's own not-documented block — naming which skills and sections were searched — never by prose written to fill the gap.
Say what you verified and what you did not. -
